learningObjective: Interpret Nsight Compute warp stall reasons and translate them to actionable optimization steps.

canonicalClaims.claim: 'Long Scoreboard' is a memory-latency stall (warps waiting for global-memory loads); mitigations include improving L2 hit rate, prefetching (cp.async), and raising warps per SM to hide latency. Attacking memory traffic (better locality) reduces the source rather than hiding it.
conditions: Nsight Compute stall taxonomy on Ampere/Hopper.
Kernel legitimately accesses memory (not a synthetic benchmark).
nonImplications: Does not imply memory-latency stalls can always be eliminated.
Does not imply barriers are always bad; they can be required for correctness.

misconceptions.claim: Long Scoreboard is a compute-pipeline stall.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a memory-latency stall; the compute-pipeline stall is Wait or MIO Throttle.

misconceptions.claim: Barrier stalls are always a bug.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Correctness requires synchronization; eliminating barriers is not always feasible.

misconceptions.claim: Reducing block size always reduces Barrier stalls.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Smaller blocks may increase kernel-launch overhead and hurt occupancy without solving the barrier.

misconceptions.claim: High DRAM throughput always means memory-saturation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Saturation is at ~90%+; 45% indicates room to grow (or to reduce).
